title: Onboarding momentum playbook — 6-week sprint scripts & renewal signal hacks
content:
Purpose:
This one-pager / working playbook is a compact, experiment-focused onboarding blueprint aimed at teams that need to convert early usage into predictable adoption and surface renewal risk signals inside the first 6 weeks. Think: high-touch for technical adopters, but lean enough to run as a short sprint with measurable experiments.

When to use this playbook:
- New mid-market customers with a technical PoC or early integration (first API keys, >1k tokens/day).
- Customers that show initial product curiosity but have low feature breadth usage.
- When the goal is to get to a repeatable demo -> integration -> production milestone within 6 weeks.

Core outcomes (measurable):
- Time-to-first-meaningful-inference (goal: <7 days from provisioning).
- Two distinct production calls/week from at least one service (goal: by week 6).
- Customer health score trajectory: neutral -> positive by week 4 (see tracker below).
- Renewal signal flags (early): low-engagement OR stalled integration OR billing disputes.

Sprint cadence (6-week):
- Week 0 (pre-sprint): provisioning, stakeholder alignment, quick tech intake.
- Weeks 1–2: accelerate adoption (fast wins, sample app, integration pairing).
- Weeks 3–4: productization (run simple evals, guardrails, routing decisions).
- Weeks 5–6: operationalize + QBR-lite (metrics, cost estimation, renewal readiness).

Week 0: pre-onboard checklist (owner = CSM / Solutions Eng)
- Provision keys + sample project repo shared (owner: SE).
- Slack channel or dedicated thread created + invited stakeholders.
- Basic plan: map primary use-case(s), minimum success criteria, security constraints.
- Ticket created in Jira/Customer board for integration blockers (tag: cs-onboard).
- Send kickoff email template (see Templates section).

Week 1: momentum (owner = SE + CSM)
- Day 1: PoC environment validated (connectivity, keys, sample call).
- Day 3: Live pairing session to run first end-to-end call + observe latency/behaviour.
- Deliverable: working example integration (documented) and screenshot of successful run.
- Quick experiment: enable prefix cache for repeated prompts — measure latency improvement.

Week 2: expand & embed (owner = CSM)
- Drive 3 different prompt variants to test robustness (edge-case prompts).
- Collect 10 qualitative sample responses and note any regressions.
- Run a short cost-estimate calculation and share token burn chart (via Console).
- Experiment: try a lower-cost quantized model variant on a subset of requests.

Week 3: reliability & metrics (owner = SRE/CSM)
- Add basic observability hooks: trace ids, sample capture, rate limit behavior.
- Run a 24–48h load smoke test to validate autoscaling/batching on Dedicated or Hosted.
- Identify 1–2 reliability improvements (timeouts, retries) and create tickets.

Week 4: quality & governance (owner = Product/CSM)
- Execute simple evals against a golden prompt set (pass/fail thresholds).
- Discuss data handling, KMS needs, audit log cadence for Private deployments.
- Experiment: flip on function-calling for structured outputs where appropriate.

Week 5: cost & rollout plan (owner = CSM + Finance Ops)
- Build a baseline cost model for steady state (tokens/per 1000 requests).
- Recommend batching/caching knobs and expected savings.
- Prepare QBR-lite slides: usage trend, latency, error rate, cost projection.

Week 6: QBR-lite + renewal readiness (owner = CSM + AM)
- Run 30-minute alignment QBR with customer: discuss accomplishments, open risks, success criteria for renewal.
- Confirm executive sponsor and internal champions for next 90 days.
- If renewal >= 6 months away, set cadence for monthly checkpoint; if <90 days, move to renewal playbook.

Experiment bank (pick 1–2 per sprint):
- Model variant A/B: compare quality vs cost on a sampled workload.
- Caching experiment: prefix caching for repetitive prompts.
- Batch size tuning: raise batch size in non-latency-critical paths and measure savings.
- Eval-led guardrails: run small evals on releases to avoid regressions.

Renewal signal tracker (quick text table to paste into Jira or sheet):
- Positive signals: recurring automated calls > threshold; champion introduced to execs; productized integration (references in code).
- Neutral signals: PoC still running but no infra commitments; usage concentrated in one developer; no SLA asked.
- Negative signals (early risk flags): integration stalled >2 weeks; cost surprises; security review open >3 weeks; no ROI story.

Sample tracker (copy-paste):
| week | usage (calls/day) | key feature used | health flag | next action | owner |
| W0 | 0 | - | neutral | provisioning | SE |
| W2 | 12 | inference-api, streaming | positive | feature demo + cost review | CSM |
| W4 | 45 | reranker + caching | positive | QBR-lite prep | AM |
| W6 | 78 | production proxy traffic | positive | renewal discussion | AM/CSM |

QBR-lite agenda (30 min):
- 5m: accomplishments & topline metrics (usage, latency, errors).
- 10m: demos of what’s running in customer infra (screenshots, logs, sample outputs).
- 5m: cost & performance recommendations (batching, model suggestions).
- 5m: risks and mitigation plan (open tickets, security items).
- 5m: next steps & renewal conversation framing.

Sample outreach templates (short):
- Kickoff email subject: Redwood onboarding — next steps + pairing session
  Body (short): Hi <Name>, quick intro — attached repo + suggested times for a 60m pairing demo this week. Goal: get a full end-to-end call working and collect your initial token profile.

- Reminder Slack ping: @<customer-champion> quick nudge: want to pair on the sample integration today at 2p? we can cut down cost by toggling quantized model after the session.

Risk ledger (what to watch for):
- Long security reviews (impact: move to Private; ask for weekly sync).
- Low feature breadth (impact: reduced stickiness; run productization workshops).
- Unexpected cost spikes (impact: churn; run model switching/caching experiments).

Hand-off checklist for week 6 -> AM/renewal team:
- Documented integration repo and runbook (incl. sample calls).
- Cost baseline and recommended knobs for steady state.
- Open tickets with owners and SLAs for each.
- Signed executive confirmation of next milestone (P0: production pilot date).

Notes / book-keeping:
- Use tags: cs-onboard, cs-experiments, cs-qbr for all Jira tasks.
- Slack channel naming: cs/<customer-short>-onboard.
- Suggested internal hack: run a weekly “demo gallery” where SEs drop one production screenshot for cross-team learning.

Next steps (for this doc):
- Run this playbook with 3 live customers in a 6-week pilot, capture metrics in a shared sheet, iterate.
- Add a short form for CSMs to fill at the end of week 6 to standardize lessons learned.

Appendix: quick checklist copy for a one-pager card
- Kickoff scheduled + project repo shared
- 1st successful end-to-end call in <7 days
- 3 prompt variants tested by W2
- Cost baseline documented by W3
- QBR-lite delivered by W6

End of draft.
